analytical_question: How did Agentic AI arise, and what does that lineage justify investigating for chart review in this context?
general_et_finding: Scope: selected Agentic AI creation history with model-selected tool actions. Need: sequence processing, flexible tasks, following instructions and connecting reasoning with external observations [S1-S5], not evidence that chart review caused original emergence. Predecessors: attention supplies sequence processing, pretraining supplies adaptable language capability, human feedback refines instruction behavior, and action/API research connects models to external evidence.  Scientific and technical — FACT [S1-S5]: the packet documents attention, scaled task learning, instruction refinement and tool-mediated actions. Economic and resource — INFERENCE: large-scale models and human demonstrations imply resource requirements [S2-S3]; GAP: financing, affordability and compute-price effects are not established. Social and user-demand — INFERENCE: following instructions and accessing external information address interaction needs [S3-S5]; GAP: measured historical demand is absent. Institutional and regulatory — GAP: this packet does not establish pre-emergence institutional or regulatory causes; contemporary organizational controls cannot fill that gap. Market and competitive — FACT [S6]: an integration protocol was announced; GAP: competitive pressure, willingness to pay and commercial success are not measured. Causal synthesis — INFERENCE: research problems motivated complementary model capabilities; connecting them to tools addressed text-only limitations; later infrastructure supported accessibility. The sequence is a supported design interpretation, not proof that each historical step was inevitable or necessary. The genealogy is selective, and its nontechnical causal account remains incomplete.
application_finding: INFERENCE: text interpretation and tool observations are relevant to investigating chart critiques. Research demonstrations do not establish dependable denominator checks or supported explanations. Keep source data and reviewer reference judgments distinct from generated claims; usefulness remains an application-level hypothesis.
organization_specific_finding: SUPPLIED ASSUMPTIONS: public tables, an approved sandbox and an editor narrow the intended exposure; engineering capacity is limited. INFERENCE: investigate a small reviewed workflow, measuring correction effort rather than assuming lower stakes guarantee value. The editor requirement is not proof that every error will be caught.

evidence.claim: Attention-based sequence modeling enabled more parallel training in the reported translation experiments.
evidence.source_or_reference: [S1] Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need. https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762
evidence.notes: This is a language-model predecessor, not an autonomous business-workflow demonstration.

evidence.claim: A scaled autoregressive model demonstrated few-shot task performance without task-specific gradient updates.
evidence.source_or_reference: [S2] Brown et al., Language Models are Few-Shot Learners. https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165
evidence.notes: Selected benchmarks do not establish report accuracy, cost savings or current vendor quality.

evidence.claim: Human demonstrations and preferences improved instruction following; models still made simple mistakes.
evidence.source_or_reference: [S3] Ouyang et al., Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155
evidence.notes: Instruction following does not guarantee truth or safety.

evidence.claim: Interleaved reasoning and actions let models interact with external information or environments in the reported tasks.
evidence.source_or_reference: [S4] Yao et al., ReAct Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models. https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629
evidence.notes: Task-specific demonstrations are not enterprise reliability evidence.

evidence.claim: The research investigated learning when to call APIs and how to incorporate returned results.
evidence.source_or_reference: [S5] Schick et al., Toolformer Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools. https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761
evidence.notes: API use does not establish permission safety or correctness of all tool outputs.

evidence.claim: A vendor announced an open protocol for connecting AI systems with data and tools.
evidence.source_or_reference: [S6] Anthropic, Introducing the Model Context Protocol. https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol
evidence.notes: Later integration enabler; not necessary for earlier agents. Announcement and early-adopter examples do not establish market penetration.

evidence.claim: Organizational details and the four-week horizon are constructed assumptions, not field observations.
evidence.notes: No organization or business pilot was observed.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Instruction-following improvements did not eliminate mistakes [S3].
Selected research tasks do not establish chart-review reliability or tool-permission safety.
No real company, chart dataset, model benchmark, cost measurement or business pilot was evaluated.
This is a selective language-model/tool-use genealogy; other planning and software-agent lineages remain outside the packet.
Five-category coverage makes nontechnical gaps explicit but supplies no new financing, demand, institutional or competitive evidence.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in the bounded source-page claims; moderate in the proposed application connection; insufficient for actual readiness, value or full causal history. This is an assistant-authored controlled design walkthrough, not an independently executed student agent.
value_opportunity_implication: Potential benefit is reduced repetitive checking and drafting. Compare total review effort and verified error counts with the manual baseline in a future authorized evaluation; no benefit is claimed as measured.
risk_governance_implication: Public data reduce confidentiality exposure but do not remove hallucination, misleading-chart or tool-selection risk. Keep deterministic checks, provenance and editor sign-off; record failed tool actions.
recommendation_management_implication: From the creation lens, investigate a small set of public-data chart checks in the existing approved sandbox over four weeks, retaining the manual baseline and human review. This is a proposed evaluation, not a production approval or evidence of savings. Route readiness and the final deployment choice to Organizational Adoption and Adoption.
change_monitoring_triggers: Revisit if data permission, model, tool scope, report audience or reviewer availability changes.
Revisit when an authorized evaluation records factual errors, review effort and failures.
Revise history if credible original evidence contradicts a source claim; obtain same-technology evidence before judging current diffusion.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Withhold production and savings conclusions pending representative chart tests, recorded errors and review effort, and accountable-owner approval.
